acceptance_criteria.criterion: When globalInsights and repoInsights contain an insight with the same id, getRepositoryContext returns it only once
Deduplication preserves insertion order (global insights first, then unique repo-scoped additions)
When no duplicates exist, behavior is unchanged — all insights are returned
All existing tests in the repository-context test suite continue to pass

summary: Implemented insight deduplication in getRepositoryContext(): changed line 166 from a simple array spread to an O(n) dedup loop that iterates [...globalInsights, ...repoInsights], tracking seen ids in a Set<number>. Global insights take precedence (first-seen wins). The deduped array preserves insertion order.

Added 3 new test cases in a dedicated 'insight deduplication' describe block in repository-context.test.ts: (1) shared id appears exactly once, (2) insertion order is global-first then unique repo additions, (3) no-overlap case is unchanged. All 3 pass. Full test suite: 3069 tests across 101 files — all pass.

comments.note: repository-context.ts line 163: the KnowledgeStoreManager is instantiated fresh on every getRepositoryContext call. For high-traffic usage this creates repeated object allocations per request. A lightweight factory or cached instance per ledgerRoot would be a minor win, though for the current call frequency (one MCP request at a time) this is negligible.

repository-context.ts: the safeListRepositoryInsights helper swallows all errors silently (bare catch {}). This is intentional for invalid repo names (SLUG_REGEX failures), but it will also mask genuine I/O errors. A narrow catch on the specific ZodError or a typed guard would be more defensive without changing the AC.

comments.note: Lines 167–175: the dedup loop creates an intermediate [...globalInsights, ...repoInsights] spread array before iterating. If insight limits grow substantially, a two-pass approach iterating each array independently would avoid the allocation — not worth changing now.
